source.author: stat
source.text: iungunt discordes inimica in foedera dextras Belidae fratres; sed vultu mitior astat Aegyptus, Danai manifestum aggnoscere ficto ore notas pacisque malae noctisque futurae, mille dehinc species, tandem satiata voluptas praestantesque viros vocat ad sua praemia virtus.
source.text_original: iungunt discordes inimica in foedera dextras / Belidae fratres; sed vultu mitior astat / Aegyptus, Danai manifestum aggnoscere ficto / ore notas pacisque malae noctisque futurae, / mille dehinc species, tandem satiata voluptas / praestantesque viros vocat ad sua praemia virtus.
source.text_english: The sons of Belus, though at odds, join their hostile hands in alliance; but Aegyptus stands there with a gentler face, and with feigned expression the Danaans openly recognize the signs of a peace that is false and of an evil night to come, and then a thousand other aspects; at last, once pleasure has had its fill, virtue calls the outstanding men to its own rewards.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: tum iuvenem tranquilla tuens nec fronte timendus occupat et fictis dat vultum et pondera dictis.
reuse.text_original: tum iuvenem tranquilla tuens nec fronte timendus / occupat et fictis dat vultum et pondera dictis.
reuse.text_english: then, gazing upon the youth with a calm expression that gave no cause for fear, he takes him in, and lends both countenance and weight to his feigned words.
